channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-web-security
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: Wakaru — via awesome-web-security
item.description: JavaScript decompiler that splits production bundles from webpack, esbuild, Browserify, and Metro into modules and turns minified and transpiled code back into readable JavaScript, without executing it, by @pionxzh.

item.title: Passive OS Fingerprinting: TCP Fingerprint, p0f and JA4T — via awesome-web-security
item.description: How the first TCP SYN gives away the operating system family, why a proxy shows up as a mismatch with the OS the browser reports, and how p0f and JA4T record the same packet. Written by packet.guru.

item.title: ONUS — via awesome-web-security
item.description: Web vulnerability assessment platform that orchestrates multiple scanners, applies deterministic CVSS v3.1 scoring, and provides AI-assisted vulnerability analysis and remediation guidance.

item.title: Instance Metadata Abuse — via awesome-web-security
item.description: Shows how a server-side request forgery bug becomes cloud credential theft through the instance metadata service, and why requiring IMDSv2 session tokens with a response hop limit in the instance configuration closes the whole class of forging bugs rather than one code path, by RansomLeak.

item.title: How to revoke a JWT, from a system that does it — via awesome-web-security
item.description: A per-user revocation cut-off from a production multi-tenant app: why it compares against auth_time rather than iat, the whole-seconds rounding bug it shipped with, and the routes that trusted the token. Written by Ridam Agrawal.

item.title: Crossfyre Toolchain — via awesome-web-security
item.description: Recon and vulnerability scanning engines in Rust for subdomains, ports, content discovery, fingerprinting, injection testing and nuclei-style templates, with one CLI and newline-delimited JSON output by @clickswave.

item.title: From DNS Evidence to a Finding: DNS and Mail Security Methodology — via awesome-web-security
item.description: How DNSSEC, DANE, SPF/DKIM/DMARC and SMTP transport evidence becomes a finding, with the decision logic for each, the dig invocations to reproduce it independently, and the false positives to expect.

item.title: XSS without HTML: Client-Side Template Injection with AngularJS — via awesome-web-security
Where the LLM Stops: Deterministic Scoring in an AI-Assisted VAPT Pipeline — via awesome-web-security
item.description: Technical write-up on designing an AI-assisted VAPT pipeline with deterministic CVSS scoring, passive confidence verification, and LLM-generated vulnerability explanations and remediation.

item.title: What is a Side-Channel Attack ? — via awesome-web-security
The 200 That Proved Nothing — via awesome-web-security
item.description: Why a 200 OK is not proof of an access-control bug: a seeded BOLA benchmark where a model asked to confirm a secure endpoint 79 times and a downgrade-only code gate refused every one, plus the similarity thresholds, a deterministic check that failed the same way, and a plausible fix measured and rejected for making results worse.
